name: Sticker Saga Cast
oneLine: Blocky R6 bodies with oversized anime hair and flat line-art face decals; every featured person gets a colour-coded name sticker and a new face every close-up.
head: Classic Roblox head (Cast v2 'classic' mesh, rounded block), 1.2 x 1.2 studs. No 3D eyes or sculpted features. Head block is 23% of standing height; with hair it reads as 30-34%.
face: Flat 2D decal, thin black ink lines (3-4 px at 1024 texture), no shading, no gloss. Features sit in the lower 60% of the face (eyes at 55% down the head, mouth at 78%). Two families: 'line faces' (dot/round eyes, single-stroke mouth) for most boys, adults and crowds; 'anime-lite faces' (half-lid eyes with a coloured iris, lash line, thin arched brows, tiny mouth) for featured characters.
eyes: Round white eyes with small black pupils (alarm), two short horizontal dashes (bored/sleepy), half-lid lash line over a coloured iris (cool/smug), ^ ^ arcs (happy), single dots (blank). Eye width ~16% of head width, spacing ~40% of head width centre to centre. One white highlight dot only on the anime-lite family.
mouth: Single ink stroke: flat line, small smile arc, smirk (one-sided), small 'o', open D-shape with dark fill (shout/shock), teeth bar (gritted). Width 15-30% of head width.

proportions.headToHeight: 0.23 head block alone (teen/adult R6); 0.30-0.34 with hair; kid/flashback variant 0.28-0.30 head block
proportions.shoulderToHead: shoulder span (torso + both arms) = 3.2-3.3 x head width; torso alone = 1.6-1.7 x head width; hair silhouette = 1.3-1.8 x head width
proportions.limbs: arms and legs are blocks 1 stud thick (half the torso width), arm length = torso height (2 studs); legs 38% of height on teens/adults, 32% on kids
proportions.note: Measured on full-body frames, matched to the R6 rig. Hair adds 0.3-0.5 head heights.

bodyTypes: kid 0.8 scale for flashbacks and little siblings
elder (bald or bun, glasses, slight stoop pose)
hair: Oversized anime hair meshes are the identity of each character: dense black spikes for the hero, long straight or twin-tail hair for featured girls, a heavy fringe that covers the top third of the face, bobs, slicked side-parts for adults. Hair is 1.3-1.8 x head width and adds 0.3-0.5 head heights on top. Texture: flat base colour plus darker painted strand strokes (dashed lines along the flow) and one soft highlight band; roughness 0.6, no gloss.
clothing: Layered everyday uniforms read in one glance: blazer + bow + plaid skirt, black hoodie or tee with a big white graphic print, tracksuit with stripes, green knit jumper for a parent. One dominant outfit colour per person, prints big enough to read at phone size, chains or belts as extra silhouette detail.
accessories: pointed elf-style ears for magical folk
satchel or box carried on the back
sweat-drop and anger-mark stickers (2D overlays, not geometry)
materials: Skin and bodies: smooth plastic (roughness 0.5, specular 0.3), no subsurface. Faces: unlit-looking decal (mix the face PNG over skin colour, no bump). Clothes: flat colour + printed graphic, light weave bump 0.1. Special states change the WHOLE avatar material in one cut (all-grey stone with ink crack lines, all-desaturated for flashback).
motion: Standard game-style rigid-limb animation: idle sway, walk, run, sit, lie down, point, arms-up flinch, hands-over-face, kneel. Poses change between shots more than inside them. Inside a held shot: one quick reaction (head turn, flinch, arm raise, ~6-8 frames) then idle. Impacts are physical: the body falls flat (ragdoll-style) and the camera stays still.
distinctCharactersPerVideo: 3-5 featured people (hero + 1-2 featured girls/rivals + 1-2 adults) plus 6-20 background extras
toldApartBy: hair silhouette and colour first, outfit colour second, accessory third (glasses, ears, bow), and a colour-coded name sticker the first time each one appears
recipe: Start from Cast v2 person() with head='classic' (classic Roblox head mesh); keep tw=2, td=1, th=2, lh=2, aw=1, al=2 for teens/adults; use s=0.8 and hs=1.15 for kids.

Face: draw a new flat line-art PNG (1024x1024, transparent, 3-4 px ink) in one of the two families, with the eyes 55% down the PNG and the mouth 78% down; it maps 1:1 with head_mat2 at the default voff=0 (person() does not pass voff; a positive voff moves the features down). Make the full 8-10 expression set for every featured person; swap per close-up with set_face() from pack/style_fourth_style.py.

Hair: build or pick an oversized hair mesh (1.3-1.8 x head width, +0.3-0.5 head heights); give it a flat base colour plus a painted strand-stroke texture and one highlight band; tint with tint_hair().
Outfit: fabric() with one dominant colour per person; add one big readable print or trim (crest, stripe, belt) and one silhouette accessory.
Pick a name-sticker colour for the character (teal, coral, gold, sky blue, lilac) and record it with the character, so every film uses the same one.
Materials: plastic skin (roughness 0.5); no outlines on the 3D model; no blush by default (Jake rejected blush on the puppet heads), use a sweat drop or anger mark sticker instead.
Make a turnaround still plus the expression strip and send it to Claude before use (only Claude adds new characters).
